# Historical rebuild schemas

`schema-history-through-20.json` preserves the earlier frozen definitions. `schema-history-through-21.json` extends that history with schema21 reconciliation request storage, leaving every prior definition/hash unchanged. The current fixture freezes SQL definitions for schemas1–21 as they existed on September 11, 2026. Definitions were captured once from the authorized rebuild migration sources; each has a SHA-256. Tests reconstruct old encrypted stores from this retained history without invoking the current migration runner, then invoke current `Store::open` to upgrade them. Verification does not regenerate this fixture. Preserve existing entries when adding future versions.

`crates/nuncio-engine/tests/support/historical_store.rs` supplies synthetic Google/IMAP accounts, original MIME/PDF blobs, mail/search/calendar rows, local drafts, queued send/request identities, configuration and legacy SMTP intent where those tables exist. Migration tests compare all pre-existing columns in every user table, excluding the advancing migration ledger and internal FTS shadow tables; public reads and payload bytes are checked separately. The snapshot is schema history, not an independently sourced provider fixture. The same historical schemas are restored from separately passphrase-keyed backup fixtures into new encrypted stores. Pending sends are held, old credential references are cleared, immutable columns/payloads are retained, and original backup bytes remain unchanged. Tests reject missing draft/operation tables once the declared schema requires them. The actual subprocess migration suite separately exercises42 SIGKILL boundaries (schema21 gate in progress), immediately before/after every commit including schema0 initialization, plus two normal restarts per case. The historical_operation_history suite enriches schemas10–21 with all send states, attempts, separate positive receipts, decisions and SMTP progress. Restore preserves those records while closing unfinished attempts and holding pending operations. Other write-kind histories and recovery lifecycle crashes still need separate coverage.

`legacy-message.eml` is a frozen 1,424-byte MIME message generated by Python’s standard email library with the real PDF above. Both Python decoding and the Rust MIME parser must recover that exact PDF; fixture recipients are synthetic `.test` addresses.
